items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: And I played a couple of sets with Earl and Slam

ctx.x: Parker came in for threesies. And there were only a few -- the guys playing on the street were only a few of my patrons because there were a gang of musicians at the White Rose as the word spread, and the food was all gone before closing -- and I made, and I just about broke even with the kitty; I think I was $25 in there, food was much cheaper then. But I cooked for a lot of people -- I think we counted 54 guys in all.

And I'll close this by saying the following Sunday, Harold West wiped my reputation off the slate. He made pigs feet and lima beans, and ham hocks, and the likes that I had never tasted before. And I played a couple of sets with Earl and Slam, he added insult to injury of baking, from scratch, biscuits and cornbread. Whew.
